react_result.final_narrative_text: Three complementary enrichment paradigms — RaMP multi-database ORA, MetaboAnalystR KEGG PSEA, and Mummichog m/z-directed network analysis — converge on two interconnected biological themes. The dominant signal is a glutathione / cysteine-sulfur axis disruption: hypotaurine (C00519), beta-mercaptoethanol (C00928), and glutathione (C00051) collectively drive enrichment of cysteine and methionine catabolism (WP:WP4504, MUMM:methionine_and_cysteine_metabolism), sulfur amino acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1614635), trans-sulfuration (WP:WP2525), and glutathione conjugation itself (KEGG:hsa00480). RaMP reports the sulfur amino acid cluster with FDR 3.1 × 10⁻⁴ and fold-enrichment 327, while MetaboAnalystR independently ranks hsa00480 (glutathione metabolism) fourth at p = 0.085, and Mummichog reports the methionine/cysteine network at p = 0.016. The second theme is drug/xenobiotic metabolism, anchored by 6-methylthiopurine (C16614, the active metabolite of azathioprine), coumarin (C05851), benzo[a]pyrene-7,8-dihydrodiol-9,10-oxide (C14853), and N-hydroxy-4-aminobiphenyl (C20319). RaMP identifies biological oxidations (REACT:R-HSA-211859, FDR 1.2 × 10⁻⁶) and azathioprine ADME (REACT:R-HSA-9748787, FDR 1.4 × 10⁻⁴) as top hits; Mummichog independently hits xenobiotics metabolism (p = 0.016). MetaboAnalystR confirms azathioprine ADME-adjacent purine metabolism (hsa00983, p = 0.117) with 6-methylthiopurine as the sole hit. 3-Aminopropionaldehyde (C05665) and hypotaurine additionally implicate the glycine/serine/alanine cluster and taurine/hypotaurine degradation, consistent with shared sulfur intermediates. The absence of FELLA (runtime error) does not compromise the consensus, which rests on two independent ORA tools plus m/z-directed network analysis. All cross-tool KEGG ↔ ChEBI ↔ HMDB IDs for glutathione, hypotaurine, 3-aminopropanal, 6-methylthiopurine, and coumarin reconcile to identical InChIKey block-14 identifiers with no structural conflicts, confirming the findings are not namespace artefacts.

react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-enrichment paradigms converged on xenobiotic metabolism and phase-I/II biotransformation as the dominant biological signal. RaMP-DB ORA (multi-DB) ranked REACT:R-HSA-211859 (Biological oxidations) at the top with FDR 1.24e-06 and four input metabolites hit (coumarin, 3-aminopropanal, 6-methylthiopurine, glutathione); Metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1430728, FDR 1.61e-06) and Metabolism of amino acids and derivatives (REACT:R-HSA-71291, FDR 9.41e-05) followed. Mummichog m/z-direct analysis independently surfaced Methionine and cysteine metabolism (rank 3, p=0.0087) and Xenobiotics metabolism (rank 2, p=0.0087) alongside Histidine metabolism, all with glutathione and hypotaurine as network hits. Coumarin and 3-aminopropanal were the primary drivers of the Biological oxidations hit by RaMP, with coumarin's InChIKey ZYGHJZDHTFUPRJ directly matching the input. Sulfur amino-acid metabolism also appeared across paradigms: Degradation of cysteine and homocysteine (REACT:R-HSA-1614558, FDR 0.000138) and Sulfur amino acid metabolism (REACT:R-HSA-1614635, FDR 0.000309) in RaMP, and Methionine and cysteine metabolism in mummichog. Cross-paradigm consensus identifies phase-I/II oxidation and sulfur amino-acid catabolism as the perturbed pathways, with coumarin, 3-aminopropanal, hypotaurine, and glutathione as the driver compounds.
